Package com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp

Class UsmSecurity

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp.UsmSecurity
public final class UsmSecurity extends Object
The cryptographic core of the SNMPv3 User-based Security Model (USM, RFC 3414). It turns a human passphrase into the per-engine localized key and produces the truncated HMAC that fills the msgAuthenticationParameters field of an authenticated message.

Everything here is pure, deterministic and JDK-only (no external crypto provider), so it is fully unit-testable offline against the published RFC 3414 Appendix A test vectors. The three steps are:

  • passwordToKey(com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp.UsmSecurity.AuthProtocol, java.lang.String) — the §A.2 password-to-key KDF: the passphrase is cycled to fill exactly 1048576 bytes (1 MB) which is then hashed once to yield the user key Ku.
  • localizeKey(com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp.UsmSecurity.AuthProtocol, byte[], byte[]) — the §2.6 key localization: Kul = digest(Ku || engineId || Ku), binding the key to a single authoritative engine.
  • authParameters(com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp.UsmSecurity.AuthProtocol, byte[], byte[]) — the HMAC auth digest (HMAC-MD5-96 / HMAC-SHA-96) of the whole message under Kul, truncated to the first 12 bytes.

Privacy (encryption) is out of scope here; this class only covers the auth side of USM.

  • Method Details

    • passwordToKey

      public static byte[] passwordToKey(UsmSecurity.AuthProtocol authProtocol, String password)
      Derives the user key Ku from password using the RFC 3414 §A.2 KDF: the passphrase bytes (UTF-8) are repeated to fill a stream of exactly 1048576 bytes which is hashed once with the protocol digest. The result is 16 bytes for MD5 and 20 bytes for SHA-1.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if authProtocol or password is null, or the password is empty (the cycling stream would be undefined)

    • localizeKey

      public static byte[] localizeKey(UsmSecurity.AuthProtocol authProtocol, byte[] key, byte[] engineId)
      Localizes a user key key to the authoritative engine engineId per RFC 3414 §2.6, i.e. Kul = digest(key || engineId || key). The localized key is what actually keys the HMAC.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if any argument is null

    • authParameters

      public static byte[] authParameters(UsmSecurity.AuthProtocol authProtocol, byte[] localizedKey, byte[] wholeMessage)
      Computes the msgAuthenticationParameters value for wholeMessage: the HMAC of the message under localizedKey, truncated to the first 12 bytes (HMAC-MD5-96 / HMAC-SHA-96).

      Per RFC 3414 §6.3.1 the digest is computed over the message with the auth-parameters field already present and zero-filled; the returned 12 bytes are spliced back into that field.

      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if any argument is null

    • passwordToLocalizedKey

      public static byte[] passwordToLocalizedKey(UsmSecurity.AuthProtocol authProtocol, String password, byte[] engineId)
      Convenience that chains passwordToKey(com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp.UsmSecurity.AuthProtocol, java.lang.String) and localizeKey(com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp.UsmSecurity.AuthProtocol, byte[], byte[]): derive Ku from the passphrase and localize it to engineId in one call.
